turns.t: Good morning. Let me be precise: I have a painful bump on the side of my right big toe, which is worse in shoes.
Thank you. How long has it been there?
The bump, about three years. The pain, the last four months, since I started a job on my feet.
What sort of pain?
Sharp, rubbing, and a throb by the end of the day. And the skin over it is red and sore.
What shoes make it worse?
Anything narrow. Work shoes, and heels. In trainers, it's bearable.
Any numbness, tingling, or burning in the toe?
No numbness. No tingling.
Any swelling of the whole toe, or heat, or discharge from the skin?
No, nothing like that. Just the bump, and the redness around it.
Let me ask you to take your shoe and sock off, and I'll have a look. ~
Of course.
There's a bony prominence at the base of the toe, and the toe is angled inwards, which is a bunion, and the skin over it is pink where the shoe rubs. ~
I thought so. Is it genetic? ~
Partly, yes. Narrow shoes make it worse, but they're not the cause. ~
Will I need surgery? ~
Not necessarily. Surgery is only for pain that doesn't respond to other measures, and it takes months to recover from. ~
I'd rather avoid that. ~
Most people do. First, wider shoes with a deeper toe box, soft insoles, and a gel pad over the bump.
Where do I get those? ~
Any pharmacy, and a good shoe shop will fit them for you. ~
And the heels? ~
Keep them for special occasions only.
That's fair. ~
Ice it for ten minutes after a long day, and keep your toes moving. ~
Right. ~
If it's still bothering you after two months of that, or the toe gets red and hot, or the skin breaks, come back and I'll refer you to the foot specialist.
I'll do that. Thank you, doctor. ~
Good luck with the new shoes. ~
